title: Best WooCommerce Developers (2026): How to Hire One
description: How to hire a WooCommerce developer: what the store project should include, how to brief it, what drives the price and red flags.
intro: WooCommerce turns a WordPress site into an online store that you fully control, from products and payments to shipping and taxes. That flexibility also means more can go wrong: plugin conflicts, slow pages and checkout errors. Projects go wrong when payment and shipping settings are not tested, or too many plugins are added. This guide shows you what to ask for.

faq.q: Is WooCommerce the right choice for my store?
faq.a: It suits businesses that already use WordPress, want full control or need custom features. If you want less maintenance, a hosted platform like Shopify may be simpler. Ask the developer to explain the trade-offs.

faq.q: Which payment gateways can I use?
faq.a: Many, depending on your country, such as Stripe, PayPal and local providers. Open the payment accounts in your own name and connect them yourself or with the developer.
Usually a few, for payments, shipping or subscriptions. Each plugin adds maintenance. Ask for a list with the purpose and cost of each.
It depends on hosting, theme, images and plugins. Ask the developer to test speed on a phone, especially product and checkout pages.

faq.q: Who maintains the store after launch?
faq.a: WordPress, WooCommerce and plugins need regular updates. Decide who does this, and read our website maintenance guide for what a plan should cover.
